plan: For capital preservation, sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, MSFU, PLTU) to zero.
Trim SPY to 20% to meet the single name concentration mandate.
This plan prioritizes safety and reduces overall portfolio risk.
It aims for a steady, low-drawdown approach.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets a modest ~1.5%/month return, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and lowering concentration, leading to lower expected volatility and drawdown.

plan: For risk-first growth, sell leveraged ETFs (METU, MSFU, SOXL, PLTU, SPAL, MUU) to reduce overall leverage.
Trim SPY to 25% to meet the single name concentration mandate.
Buy SPXS at 4% as a strong scanner setup to add exposure.
This plan balances broad index exposure with quality tech and a small amount of new leverage.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for ~2.5%/month growth, prioritizing risk management. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while adding a high-quality scanner setup. Expect moderate volatility and drawdown.

plan: For aggressive growth, trim SPY to 25% to meet the single name concentration mandate.
Buy SPXS at 6%, NVDD at 6%, and AAPU at 6% to concentrate in high-scoring scanner setups.
This plan leans into leverage and concentration for higher potential returns.
It uses strict stops to manage increased risk.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4%/month growth by leveraging high-scoring setups and increasing concentration. Be aware of significantly higher potential drawdown and the daily decay/rebalancing of leveraged ETFs. Strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: For income, sell all high-beta and leveraged names (METU, MSFU, SOXL, PLTU, SPAL, MUU) to near zero.
Trim SPY to 20% to meet the single name concentration mandate.
Add QQQI to 30% to increase exposure to income-generating ETFs.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1%/month, focusing on reliable monthly distributions and low drawdown. It significantly reduces growth potential and high-beta exposure. Remember, distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in market downturns.
